review.scope: Full eight-contender causal projection and common comparison; targeted source-recovered personnel, election-constituency and Afghan-order review. Remaining issue calendars, filings and seven-day recall incomplete.

administration.headline: Defeat opens competing paths: executive confrontation, departmental control and incoming oversight.
administration.summary: Trump retains executive authority after the midterm defeat. Miller’s prospective gatekeeping gain points toward confrontation, while Justice Department departures create room for Blanche to consolidate management; neither establishes a uniform policy turn. Incoming Democratic majorities gain oversight and funding leverage after organization. Costs, responsibility and who can credibly correct them remain central. Court constraints are specific: the recovered Afghan order protects identified clients beyond the former cutoff. A permitted correction could preserve an heir’s coalition, while continuing failure could help rivals build new ones. Other policy and court findings remain carried where not freshly checked.

contests.title: White House access is shifting
contests.assessment: Miller’s announced promotion promises broader access for the Maximalists. Wiles’s move changes the Operation’s White House role; it does not establish a transfer of campaign-money control.
contests.authority: Trump appoints the chief of staff. The reported handover is November 9.
contests.leverage: Miller gains a prospective agenda channel; Wiles retains a reported political-operation role.
contests.change: Appointment announced; exercised authority still pending.

basis.actions: Trump named Miller to succeed Wiles.
basis.positions: Public congratulations preserve unity; they establish no 2028 endorsement.
basis.money: No financial cause for the appointment is established. Campaign resources and White House access are separate channels.

contests.watch: Confirm the handover and each adviser’s actual remit.
contests.summary: Miller is positioned to gain agenda access. Wiles’s political remit and the November 9 handover remain to be verified.

contests.title: Iran policy remains a contested decision
contests.assessment: Vance has a negotiating channel and a public case for ending the war. Rubio’s defense of Trump supplies a rival position. Neither establishes control over Trump’s next military decision or a completed settlement.
contests.authority: Trump directs military decisions; Congress controls appropriations and has war powers.
contests.leverage: Negotiators influence the options. Public criticism changes political positioning before it changes policy.
contests.change: A visible split over the war’s political costs; the policy outcome remains open.

basis.actions: Trump reviewed options; Vance has led negotiations.
basis.positions: Vance publicly blamed the war for electoral losses; Rubio defended Trump’s decision.
basis.money: Deal-Capital’s business exposure is relevant context, not proof of donor direction of negotiations.

contests.watch: Look for an order, observable operational change or an accepted agreement.
contests.summary: Vance’s negotiating role competes with hawkish arguments; Trump retains the military decision.

contests.title: The succession coalition is still open
contests.assessment: Vance has the clearest recorded organizational route. Rubio retains a competing institutional and donor lane. Trump has not settled the succession question in the reviewed record.
contests.authority: Republican voters and the nomination process decide the nominee. Trump’s support is an influential endorsement channel.
contests.leverage: Party fundraising, organizations, donor access and public positioning supply distinct forms of leverage.
contests.change: Vance’s post-election argument separates him from hawkish rivals without demonstrating a gain in voter support.

basis.actions: The RNC finance role, Malik fundraiser and Turning Point backing are concrete channels.
basis.positions: Public deferral, message support and a candidate endorsement mean different things.
basis.money: Thiel’s historical backing and Rockbridge access help explain Vance’s network; Griffin’s reported preference is not a Rubio contribution pledge.

contests.watch: Track entry intentions, endorsements, organizing and new support evidence.
contests.summary: Vance has the clearest organizational route. Rubio retains a competing donor and institutional lane.

contests.title: Fed governance has institutional limits
contests.assessment: White House pressure on Cook remains constrained by legal process. Treasury’s policy influence must be distinguished from the FOMC’s authority over rates.
contests.authority: The FOMC votes on rates. Removal disputes involve the presidency and courts under the applicable law.
contests.leverage: Advisers can shape pressure and process; that does not give a faction control over the rate vote.
contests.change: Cook’s hearing schedule and process remain unresolved in the reviewed coverage.

basis.actions: The hearing was delayed; the later filing addressed scheduling and participation.
basis.positions: Calls for lower rates do not establish a changed vote or removal.
basis.money: Market exposure can explain interests; no payment causing a rate decision is established.

contests.watch: Verify the hearing notice, court disposition and any action actually taken.
contests.summary: White House pressure is constrained by legal process. Rate authority remains with the FOMC.

contests.title: Justice Department management is changing
contests.summary: Departures create an opening for Blanche to consolidate management; the program’s direction remains unresolved.
contests.assessment: My reading: turnover changes particular enforcement channels before proving any broader retreat. Acting replacements could sustain the program.
contests.authority: The attorney general directs the department; appointments, acting authority and confirmations follow separate processes.
contests.leverage: Department leadership can replace managers and redirect resources; former officials remain exposed to future oversight.
contests.change: Three leadership departures reported; successors and any operational changes unverified.

basis.actions: Dated CNN account of the departures.
basis.positions: No new public policy reversal established.
basis.money: Possible professional incentives are distinct from documented departure reasons; no payment causing the changes is established.

contests.watch: Confirm successors, acting roles, case continuity and actual policy instructions.

nomination.headline: Vance leads; future coalition building widens the contest.
nomination.summary: The weekly causal review retains the five environments while revising candidate conversion assumptions. First-term program continuity can offer an emerging contender a route without assigning current-policy immunity. State approval does not guarantee national entry or a high floor. Vance keeps the strongest recorded starting route, with governors and restraint contenders competing for overlapping openings. This is a model correction, not measured post-election support.

candidates.path: Current succession channels justify a lead, but cannot guarantee retention when a credible rival mobilizes program-continuity voters. Retain the largest recovery/backlash shares while reducing systemic insulation.
candidates.coalition: RNC fundraising, Rockbridge and Turning Point channels.
candidates.vulnerability: Post-defeat criticism looks retrospective. Documents or a Hegseth confrontation force him to defend conduct he privately questioned, abandon a colleague, or evade. Rivals use that record to make both loyalty and restraint claims untrustworthy.
candidates.positions: Economic nationalism, immigration restriction and a negotiating role.
candidates.money: Historical Thiel backing; access does not imply agreement on every policy.

candidates.path: Retain the security/continuity lane: independent entry is uncertain but institutional resources are mobilizable. Neither a public denial nor current responsibility makes the path zero; no automatic donor transfer from Vance.
candidates.coalition: State/NSC relationships and donors who prefer him.
candidates.advantage: National visibility and an existing policy network.
candidates.vulnerability: If the policy itself is repudiated, credentials become ownership. Hearings put his explanations alongside internal warnings, while deference to Vance or failure to enter prevents conversion of donor preference into a campaign.
candidates.positions: Hawkish commitments coexist with deference to Trump.
candidates.money: Griffin preference and prospective donor interest are not pledged 2028 funds.

candidates.path: Keep the leading executive-reset route while allowing competitors to form. National campaign experience helps rebuilding without proving voters like him or guaranteeing all reset resources.
candidates.coalition: Social conservatives and voters seeking distance from Washington.
candidates.advantage: Executive experience outside the federal decision chain.
candidates.vulnerability: Distance is mistaken for popularity. His earlier intervention statements, state accountability exposure and past campaign problems prevent a clean break, while donors prefer someone outside the approved roster.
candidates.positions: Enacted state policies; support for limited strikes complicates a restraint pitch.
candidates.money: Past fundraising capacity is not a verified current donor coalition.

candidates.path: A developed ideological and donor-facing route survives all environments. Modestly improve recovery competitiveness; do not cap him solely for a prior loss or assume he captures the governors’ whole lane.
candidates.coalition: Religious conservatives and overlapping hawkish networks.
candidates.advantage: A recognizable policy identity and donor-facing lane.
candidates.vulnerability: A hawkish record limits separation from intervention, Rubio competes for donors and recognition does not produce coalition growth. Past repositioning and judgment controversies remain usable.
candidates.positions: Hawkish foreign policy and tariff skepticism distinguish his pitch.
candidates.money: Historical presidential donors do not establish present commitments.

candidates.path: Remove the inherited 1–3 ceiling: first-term program continuity can compete with second-term exposure, and enthusiasm, personnel relationships and acquired election specialists can reinforce one another. Entry, association with later planning, commercial scrutiny and voter conversion still make him a long shot.
candidates.coalition: Hypothesized younger, culturally conservative Trump-aligned audience seeking program continuity with different leadership; voter composition and conversion remain unverified.
candidates.advantage: Historical personnel recruitment and withdrawal work can combine with future enthusiasm and acquired electoral staff; this is a prospective conversion path.
candidates.vulnerability: Entry, political funding and a measured constituency remain unknown. Later planning ties, business scrutiny and personal-record attacks can defeat separation from current leadership.
candidates.positions: Historical restrictionist staffing and withdrawal advocacy; current specifics need review.
candidates.money: Thiel’s dating-business investment is not a nomination endorsement.

candidates.path: A developed constitutional-limit route remains stronger than attention alone, but Paul cannot own the entire restraint pool. Preserve meaningful upside while allocating competition from Massie and program-continuity challengers.
candidates.coalition: Liberty-oriented conservatives and a potential free-trade business constituency.
candidates.advantage: A policy identity with dissent predating the defeat.
candidates.vulnerability: A narrow constituency, overlapping Massie support and an undecided run.
candidates.positions: Fiscal restraint, free trade and constitutional limits; current immigration specifics remain open.
candidates.money: Historical Protect Freedom/Yass ties are not confirmed 2028 commitments.

candidates.path: Reduce the automatic national floor from home-state approval. A state network is a genuine asset and can grow, but needs entry, national appeal and early-state conversion, especially when loyalty dominates.
candidates.coalition: A strong Georgia foundation and potential electability-focused conservative support.
candidates.advantage: Executive experience outside federal war decisions.
candidates.vulnerability: Home-state standing requires national conversion; entry, personality appeal and competition with other executives prevent a guaranteed national floor.
candidates.positions: State tax relief and enacted enforcement/social policies; no complete federal platform is assumed.
candidates.money: No current presidential donor commitments verified in this review.

candidates.path: Increase accountability upside without assuming a primary defeat permanently blocks national growth. A GOP route and acquired organization remain necessary; independent presidential support cannot count as Republican nomination success.
candidates.coalition: Libertarian and restraint-oriented audiences overlapping Paul’s.
candidates.advantage: Specific oversight and war-powers acts before the defeat.
candidates.vulnerability: Primary loss, national organization and possible non-GOP route limit the nomination path.
candidates.positions: Congressional war authorization and executive accountability; other current policy gaps remain labeled.
candidates.money: Historical independent House-primary support is not presidential campaign money.

recovery.title: The Iran war eases and lower living costs restore support for Trump
recovery.summary: Fighting related to Iran decreases and households see sustained relief in living expenses. Republican voters give Trump and candidates associated with him more credit, despite continuing scrutiny.

managed_costs.title: Voters stay unhappy, but Trump’s allies keep donors and campaign support
managed_costs.summary: Voters remain dissatisfied with the war and living costs. Trump-aligned candidates keep enough donor support, staff and activists to compete, while challengers struggle to unite unhappy Republicans.

systemic.title: Policy failures or scandals turn Republicans against Trump’s leadership
systemic.summary: Continuing policy failures or credible disclosures persuade a meaningful share of Republican voters to blame Trump and senior administration figures. Candidates outside the current federal leadership have an opening to recruit those voters, donors and campaign staff.

selective.title: Republicans blame specific officials but still back a Trump-aligned successor
selective.summary: Republican voters accept that particular officials, rather than the whole administration, are responsible for failures. A Trump-aligned candidate can promise changes without breaking with Trump.

backlash.title: Republicans rally behind Trump against Democratic investigations
backlash.summary: Investigations produce little that persuades Republican voters, or are seen as partisan. Opposition to Democrats restores support for Trump-aligned candidates even if the war and living costs do not improve.

cross_implications.title: A negotiating role is also a succession asset.
cross_implications.assessment: Vance’s war postmortem offers differentiation from hawkish rivals while his earlier public defenses retain exposure. That is strategic positioning, not a measured transfer of primary support.

cross_implications.title: New gatekeeping changes the channels contenders must navigate.
cross_implications.assessment: Miller’s announced promotion could broaden his agenda access. It supplies no evidence that he or the White House has chosen a nominee.

cross_implications.title: Managerial consolidation can coexist with confrontation.
cross_implications.assessment: Blanche is a possible overlooked beneficiary of departures while Miller gains prospective access. Recognizing those positions need not wait for a new prosecution, confirmed successor or completed policy turn.

relationships.assessment: Different post-election war arguments supply competing succession pitches. No measured support transfer is established.
The announced chief-of-staff transition changes prospective access. The handover and allocation of political responsibilities remain to be verified.
Historical backing supplies a channel into the nomination coalition. It does not establish agreement on every policy or a new 2028 pledge.

power_shifts.role_change: Chief of staff → reported political-operation role
power_shifts.implication: Less White House agenda gatekeeping; campaign-resource influence may persist.

power_shifts.role_change: Deputy chief of staff → announced chief of staff
power_shifts.implication: A broader agenda and staffing channel for enforcement hardliners; this does not itself change policy.

power_method.title: Role-based agenda access · 0–5
power_method.scale: 0 no identified channel; 1 outside access; 2 political-operation channel; 3 deputy-level White House role; 4 chief-of-staff gatekeeping; 5 presidential decision authority.
power_method.status: Conditional post-handover scenario, not an observed transfer or a calibrated measure of total faction power. Scores are ordinal analyst judgments, not percentages.
power_method.condition: The reported November 9 handover and political-operation remit must occur as described.
power_method.policy_projection: Greater hardliner access could prioritize enforcement and staffing. It does not guarantee Iran escalation: the ledger also records Miller’s reported exit pitch. Democratic oversight and funding pressure may constrain both camps.
